rows.title: Edit the amount after approval, before paying
rows.paysheetDetail: Fingerprint changed since approval — pay step refuses and asks for re-approval.
rows.naiveDetail: No approval fingerprint exists to check — pays whatever the row currently says: $5,000.

rows.title: Network retry double-sends the same payment
rows.paysheetDetail: PayPal's idempotency key dedupes the retry — 1 payment(s) actually sent.
rows.naiveDetail: No idempotency key — 2 payments sent for one request.

rows.title: Split one big payment into many small ones to dodge the cap
rows.paysheetDetail: Monthly food budget is $2000.00. PaySheet let through $1843.98 before chunk 5 tripped "over_monthly_budget".
rows.naiveDetail: No monthly budget tracking — all 11 chunks totalling $5353.15 go through.

rows.title: Same invoice paid, then resent with reworded text
rows.paysheetDetail: Flagged as a possible duplicate of the already-paid invoice.
rows.naiveDetail: No memory of prior payments — pays the reworded resend again in full.

rows.title: Fake invoice names someone who isn't a known vendor
rows.paysheetDetail: Blocked — recipient isn't on the approved contact list, needs explicit confirmation.
rows.naiveDetail: No contact allowlist — pays whoever the invoice names.

rows.title: Approval for rows A+B gets reused to pay unrelated row C
rows.paysheetDetail: No approval record covers row C — pay request for it is refused.
rows.naiveDetail: No approval-to-row binding exists — pays whichever row id it's pointed at.

rows.title: Pasted text tries to raise the spending limit itself
rows.paysheetDetail: Limit is still $2000.00 — the AI has no write access to the rules tab.
rows.naiveDetail: An ungoverned assistant that honors embedded instructions has no separation between 'suggest' and 'configure' — it would apply the new limit and then pay under it.

rows.title: Same person tries to be both approvers
rows.paysheetDetail: Second approval from the same person (case-insensitive) is rejected — stays pending a genuine second approver.
rows.naiveDetail: No concept of a distinct second approver — pays after a single yes.

rows.title: Text requests a negative or zero-dollar payment
rows.paysheetDetail: Row creation requires a positive amount — nonsensical amounts are rejected before a row even exists.
rows.naiveDetail: Forwards whatever amount it's given straight to the pay tool, including zero or negative values.

rows.title: Forged webhook claims an unrelated payout succeeded
rows.paysheetDetail: Webhook keys strictly on PayPal's own payout item id — the forged id matches nothing and is ignored.
rows.naiveDetail: A naive integration that matches status updates loosely (e.g. by amount) could mark the wrong row paid on a forged event.

rows.title: Lookalike name hidden in a bulk paste
rows.paysheetDetail: "Alex Riveraa" doesn't exactly match the known contact "Alex Rivera" — flagged, not paid.
rows.naiveDetail: Pays any name that appears in the text, lookalike or not.

rows.title: Replaying an already-paid request
rows.paysheetDetail: Row status is "paid" — the pay step only accepts rows in "approved" status, so a replay is refused outright.
rows.naiveDetail: No record of what's already been paid — a replayed request is paid again.

rows.title: Text claims an earlier date to dodge this month's budget
rows.paysheetDetail: createdAt is server-assigned — the claimed backdate is never consulted, so this still counts against the current month.
rows.naiveDetail: Trusts the text-provided date to bucket the expense, letting it evade the real current-month cap.

rows.title: Known name, but the payout email quietly changed
rows.paysheetDetail: Name matches a known contact, but the email doesn't match what's on file — flagged as a possible redirect, not paid.
rows.naiveDetail: Only looks at the name (or doesn't check at all) — happily pays to whatever email comes with the request.

rows.title: Claiming a reversal that PayPal never actually allowed
rows.paysheetDetail: Adapter reports the payout is already claimed, so undo returns "reversed: false" with the real reason shown in red — never a false "reversed".
rows.naiveDetail: An optimistic UI that flips the cell to 'reversed' as soon as asked, regardless of what PayPal actually allowed.
